title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option P3: The American West, c1835–c1895

exam_structure.overview: Tests unfolding period narrative across 3 Key Topics. Q1 Explain two consequences (8m), Q2 Write an analytical narrative (8m), Q3 Explain the importance of two events (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: The early settlement of the West, c1835–c1862

topics.title: 1. Indigenous peoples of the Plains: their beliefs and ways of life
points: Social & tribal structures, ways of life & means of survival on the Plains
Beliefs about land & nature & attitudes to war & property

topics.title: 2. Migration and early settlement
points: Factors encouraging migration (incl. the Oregon Trail from 1836, the belief in Manifest Destiny & the California Gold Rush of 1849)
Early migration to c1850 (incl. the experiences of the Donner Party & the Mormon migration, 1846–47)
Development & problems of early settlement

topics.title: 3. Conflict and tension
points: Causes of tension with Indigenous peoples of the Plains (incl. US government policy & the 'Permanent Indian Frontier'); first Fort Laramie Treaty (1851); The Indian Appropriations Act (1851)
Lawlessness in early towns & settlements (incl. a ttempts to tackle lawlessness)

sections.title: Key topic 2: Development of the Plains, c1862–c1876

topics.title: 1. The development of settlement in the West
points: Significance: railroads; the Pacific Railroad Act (1862) & the completion of the First Transcontinental Railroad (1869) & the spread of the railroad network
Impact of the Homestead Act (1862); Attempts at solutions to problems faced by homesteaders: the use of new methods & new technology; the impact of the Timber Culture Act (1873)
Introducing law & order in settlements (incl. the roles of law officers & increases in federal government influence)

topics.title: 2. Ranching and the cattle industry
points: Cattle industry & factors in its growth (incl. the roles of Iliff, McCoy & Goodnight, Abilene & of the increasing use of the railroad network)
Changing role of the cowboy (incl. changes in ranching); Relations between ranchers & homesteaders

topics.title: 3. Changes in the ways of life of Indigenous peoples of the Plains
points: Impact of railroads, the cattle industry & gold prospecting on Indigenous peoples
Impact of US government policy towards Indigenous peoples (incl. the continued use of reservations); second Fort Laramie Treaty (1868)
Conflict on the Plains: Little Crow’s War (1862) & the Sand Creek Massacre (1864), Red Cloud’s War (1866–68)

sections.title: Key topic 3: Later developments in the West, c1876–c1895

topics.title: 1. Changes in farming, the cattle industry and settlement
points: Changes in farming: the impact of new technology & new farming methods
Changes in the cattle industry (incl. winter of 1886–87); changes in the nature of ranching; T he end of the open range
Continued settlement: the Exoduster movement & Kansas (1879), the Oklahoma Land Rush of 1893; closure of the 'Indian Frontier'

topics.title: 2. Conflict and tension
points: Responses to law & order (incl. sheriffs & marshals)(incl. Billy the Kid, Wyatt Earp, the OK Corral (1881)
Range wars (incl. the Johnson County War of 1892)
Conflict on the Plains: the Battle of the Little Big Horn (1876) & its impact; the Wounded Knee Massacre ( 1890)

topics.title: 3. Indigenous peoples of the Plains: the destruction of their ways of life
points: Hunting & extermination of the buffalo
Indigenous people's lives on the reservations
Significance: changing government attitudes to Indigenous peoples (incl. the Dawes Act (1887)
